questions.subject: digital-electronics
questions.ref: Representation of Boolean Expressions and K-Maps Q1
questions.question: The minimal Sum of Products form of \(f = A \bar BCD + \bar ABC + BCD + \bar A \bar BC\) is
questions.explanation:
The function given is \(f = A \bar BCD + \bar ABC + BCD + \bar A \bar BC\) .
Method 1
The function can be minimized as: \[f = CD (A \bar B + \bar A) + \bar AC (B + \bar B ) +BCD = CD (\bar A + \bar B ) + \bar AC + BCD\] \[f = \bar A CD + \bar A C + \bar BCD + BCD = \bar A C + CD\]
Method 2
The function can be written in canonical SOP form as \[f = A \bar BCD + \bar ABC \bar D + \bar ABCD + \bar A BCD + ABCD + \bar A \bar BCD + \bar A \bar BC \bar D\] Removing repeated terms, \[f = A \bar BCD + \bar ABC \bar D + \bar A BCD + ABCD + \bar A \bar BCD + \bar A \bar BC \bar D\] The minterm indices are: \[f = \Sigma m(2,3,6,7,11,15)\] The K-Map can be drawn as: Thus the minimal SOP expression obtained is \(\bar A C + CD\) .
\[\boxed{(B)\;\bar A C + CD}\]

questions.subject: digital-electronics
questions.question: The minimum number of flipflops needed to make mod-2 counter is
questions.explanation: The minimum number of flipflops required for mod-\(N\) counter is given by \[2^n \ge N\] where \(n\) is the minimum number of flipflops. \[2^n \ge 2 \implies n =1\] \[\boxed{(A) \; 1}\]

questions.subject: digital-electronics
questions.question: The full scale input voltage to an ADC is 10 V. The resolution required is 5 mV. The minimum number of bits required for ADC is
questions.explanation:
Given:
  • Full scale voltage \(V_{fs}\) = 10 V
  • Resolution required \(\Delta\) = 5 mV
\[\Delta \; \times \text{ Number of steps = Full scale voltage}\] \[5 \times 10^{-3} \; \times \text{ Number of steps = 10 V}\] \[\text{ Number of steps = } \frac{10}{5 \times 10^{-3}} = 2 \times 10^3\] \[\text{ Number of steps } \le\; 2^n - 1\] \[2000 \le 2^n - 1 \implies n \ge 10.966 \implies n = 11\] \[\boxed{(C) \; 11}\]
Key points
  • If resolution is given in volts, it means step size (\(\Delta\)) has been given.

questions.question: The phase margin of the system for which loop gain \(GH(j\omega)=\dfrac{1}{(j\omega+1)^3}\) is
questions.explanation:
The gain crossover frequency satisfies: \[|GH(j\omega_{gc})|=1\] \[\frac{1}{(1+\omega_{gc}^2)^{3/2}}=1\] \[\omega_{gc}=0\] The phase at the gain crossover frequency is, \(\angle GH(j0)
=-3\tan^{-1}(0)
=0\) Therefore, the phase margin is: \[\mathrm{PM}
=\pi+\angle GH(j\omega_{gc})
=\pi+0
=\pi\] \[\boxed{(B)\;\pi}\]

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.question: The input error voltage to a PD-Controller, \(e(t)\) is shown in the figure. The output voltage of the controller \(e_0(t)\) is
questions.explanation:
The transfer function of an ideal PD controller is: \[G_c(s)=K(1+T_ds)\] Hence, the controller output is: \[e_o(t)=K\left[e(t)+T_d\frac{de(t)}{dt}\right]\] From the given input signal,
  • For \(0<t<1\), \(e(t)=0\).
  • For \(1<t<2\), \(e(t)\) is a ramp.
  • For \(t>2\), \(e(t)\) is constant.
img/ch10_controllers_and_compensators/10_98_1.png \[\frac{de(t)}{dt}= \begin{cases} 0, & 0<t<1,\\ \text{constant}, & 1<t<2,\\ 0, & t>2. \end{cases}\] img/ch10_controllers_and_compensators/10_98_1_3.png Hence, the controller output is obtained by adding the proportional and derivative components: img/ch10_controllers_and_compensators/10_98_1_2.png \(+\) img/ch10_controllers_and_compensators/10_98_1_3.png \(=\) img/ch10_controllers_and_compensators/10_98_1_4.png The obtained waveform is similar to option (B). \[\boxed{\text{Option (B)}}\]
